title: Gideon and the Ledger
premise: During a bitter border war's final year, Sebastian Halloran, a battlefield nurse who keeps a secret ledger of the names officers omit from official reports, is forced to shelter a child left at the hospital door with a note reading 'forget the face.' The child is the illegitimate heir of a general whose faction is rewriting the war's history, and the ledger holds the proof of atrocities the victors intend to bury. Hunted by the general's adjutant and betrayed by the one colleague Sebastian trusted, Sebastian must smuggle the ledger and the child across a collapsing front line to a neutral archive. In the end Sebastian testifies before the historians' tribunal at the cost of the anonymity they built their life on, the child's face enters the record, and the ledger is bound into the official history with every omitted name restored.
about_author: Ulyana Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed letters from twentieth-century wars. She writes historical fiction about the people official records forgot.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Sebastian Halloran, a battlefield nurse at a rear-echelon hospital, tends the wounded and privately records the names of soldiers whose deaths officers omit from dispatches. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: quiet, methodical conviction that history happens elsewhere—establishing the ledger as both ritual and shield.

chapters.title: Instructions in a Child's Hand
chapters.summary: A child of about seven is left at the hospital's back door at dawn, wrapped in a general's blanket, with a note: 'forget the face.' Sebastian, breaking protocol, keeps the child hidden rather than reporting to the commanding officer. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the first crack in Sebastian's belief in their own invisibility.

chapters.title: The Adjutant's Questions
chapters.summary: Adjutant Corvane arrives from headquarters asking after a missing child, courteous and chilling, offering Sebastian a promotion for silence. Sebastian lies for the first time in their careful life. POV: Sebastian, with a brief Corvane scene. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Remembers
chapters.summary: Sebastian reviews the ledger and realizes entries implicate General Aldous Vane—the child's father—in a massacre at Kellin Bridge that official history records as a heroic stand. POV: Sebastian, interleaved with ledger excerpts. Emotional beat: dawning understanding that the child is evidence, not just a charge.

chapters.title: Sister Amity's Bargain
chapters.summary: Head nurse Sister Amity discovers the child but, instead of reporting, reveals she lost sons to the same war and offers help—while warning that the hospital's chaplain reports directly to Corvane. POV: Amity. Emotional beat: unexpected alliance; belonging found in shared grief.

chapters.title: A Name for the Child
chapters.summary: Sebastian, who has kept everyone at arm's length, begins teaching the child—called 'Wren' for now—letters using the ledger's names as a primer. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: tenderness as risk; the ledger becomes inheritance rather than weapon.

chapters.title: Kellin Bridge
chapters.summary: A wounded survivor of Kellin Bridge, Private Odile Ferran, arrives and corroborates the ledger's account, naming officers who ordered civilians driven onto the bridge. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: testimony given voice; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Chaplain's Sermon
chapters.summary: The chaplain preaches on the sin of bearing false witness against one's superiors, staring at Sebastian; that night the hospital's records room is searched. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: surveillance closing in; the sense that the institution itself has chosen a side.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Corvane offers Sebastian passage home and immunity in exchange for the ledger and the child, revealing that the war is ending and the victors' historians arrive within weeks. POV: Corvane. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy; the reader sees his sincere belief that forgetting is a kindness.

chapters.title: Odile's Choice
chapters.summary: Sebastian asks Odile to carry the ledger's duplicate to the neutral archive at Verenne; Odile, still broken by what she saw, refuses—then changes her mind after seeing Wren sleep. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: courage as a decision made twice.

chapters.title: Fire at the Records Room
chapters.summary: A fire destroys the hospital's official records; Sebastian realizes it was set to erase the paper trail, and that the ledger is now the only surviving account. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: escalation—the enemy is no longer hiding its intent.

chapters.title: The Trusted Hand
chapters.summary: Sebastian's closest friend, orderly Tomas Reyes, betrays Wren's hiding place to Corvane to save his own brother from a treason charge. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: betrayal born of love; the cost of loyalty under power.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Ward
chapters.summary: With the hospital surrounded, Amity smuggles Wren out in a laundry cart while Sebastian creates a diversion in the ward; Amity is detained. POV: alternating Sebastian and Amity. Emotional beat: sacrifice; the mentor taken so the child can run.

chapters.title: The Road to Verenne
chapters.summary: Sebastian and Wren travel with a refugee column, the ledger sewn into Sebastian's coat; Wren asks whether forgetting the face would have kept them safe. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the road as reckoning; memory chosen over safety, out loud.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Marle
chapters.summary: A checkpoint nearly exposes them; Odile, now traveling ahead of them, creates a false lead that lets Sebastian and Wren pass—but Odile is taken. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the price of the plan compounding; guilt as fuel.

chapters.title: The General's Letter
chapters.summary: In a ruined farmhouse, Sebastian finds a letter from General Vane to Wren's mother, proving he ordered the child's erasure to protect his reputation. POV: Sebastian, reading. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the enemy's motive fully revealed as vanity dressed as duty.

chapters.title: What Wren Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren reveals memories of Kellin Bridge—faces, a song, a woman's hands—confirming the ledger from a child's eyes. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the smallest witness carrying the heaviest truth.

chapters.title: The Archive at Verenne
chapters.summary: They reach Verenne, but the archive's director hesitates—neutral means cautious—and Corvane's men arrive at the city gates with a warrant naming Sebastian a kidnapper. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: sanctuary uncertain; the law itself weaponized.

chapters.title: The Historians' Tribunal
chapters.summary: The victors' historians convene to finalize the official account; Sebastian, with the director's grudging help, gains the right to submit evidence before the record closes at midnight. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the race against erasure reaching its peak.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Sebastian reads the ledger aloud, name by name, as Odile—released and defiant—corroborates Kellin Bridge, and Wren's face is entered into the record against the note's instruction. POV: Sebastian and Odile. Emotional beat: the climax; invisibility surrendered, truth made official.

chapters.title: Corvane's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Confronted with his own signature in the ledger, Corvane breaks—not with rage but with relief, confessing that he too had wanted to remember; Vane's faction collapses. POV: Corvane. Emotional beat: the corruptor undone by the memory he enforced.

chapters.title: The Bound Volume
chapters.summary: A year later, the ledger is bound into the official history with every omitted name restored; Sebastian, no longer invisible, teaches in Verenne with Wren—now named Odile the younger—learning letters from the bound volume. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: belonging earned; memory as home.
